matches.title: Power Patron vs. Sky Striker
context: This match is preserved as a detailed tactical archive, but the exact original line-by-line transcript was not available during the final viewer migration.

games.title: Game 1

turns.title: Opening development
actions: Power Patron opens through Artmage Vandalism -Assault-, Medius the Pure, and Plundered Power Patron Plane – Vidolia.
Ash Blossom stops Medius, but Vidolia still reaches Nervedo the Shadebeast Power Patron.
The board develops into Artmage Non-Finito, Jupiter the Power Patron of Destruction, and Diactorus the DoomZ Raider with interaction behind them.
turns.audit: Multiple distinct Extra Deck bodies are kept instead of compressing into one threat.
turns.endBoard: Power Patron establishes layered interaction.

turns.title: Sky Striker counterattack
actions: Sky Striker uses Engage!, Widow Anchor, Hayate, and Zeke.
Zeke temporarily banishes Non-Finito and the borrowed Diactorus becomes Link Material.
turns.audit: Sky Striker correctly uses its Link toolbox to turn stolen monsters into permanent resource conversion.
turns.endBoard: Sky Striker dismantles most of the opening field.

turns.title: Power Patron rebuild
actions: Power Patron rebuilds into Varudras, the Final Bringer of the End Times.
Junora the Power Patron of Tuning later shuts off Shizuku before lethal.
turns.audit: The rebuild prioritizes a fresh interruption and denies Sky Striker’s end-phase recovery.
turns.endBoard: Power Patron wins Game 1.

games.decidingFactor: Power Patron’s second wave outlasts Sky Striker’s first board-breaking sequence.

games.title: Game 2

turns.title: Sky Striker setup
actions: Sky Striker opens Sky Striker Ace – Zero, Radiant Typhoon Vision, Widow Anchor, and Solemn Judgment.
turns.audit: The setup balances interruption with Link follow-up.
turns.endBoard: Sky Striker establishes a protected control board.

turns.title: Power Patron forces the board
actions: Harpie’s Feather Duster forces Solemn Judgment.
Vidolia, Medius, Jupredo, Jupiter, and Diactorus dismantle the remaining field.
turns.audit: Power Patron leads with the card most likely to force the hard negate before committing engine pieces.
turns.endBoard: Power Patron takes control.

turns.title: Sky Striker extended Link sequence
actions: Sky Striker performs Zero → S:P Little Knight → Camellia → Kagari → Hayate → Shizuku.
Power Patron is reduced to 3200 LP.
turns.audit: The sequence maximizes graveyard access and Linkage pressure.
turns.endBoard: Sky Striker nearly stabilizes.

turns.title: Final exchange
actions: Power Patron rebuilds into Varudras and Jupiter.
Lemnisgate clears both, but Nerva the Power Patron of Creation converts an Artmage trigger into the final field wipe.
turns.audit: Nerva is held for the point where Sky Striker has exhausted its Link ladder.
turns.endBoard: Power Patron wins Game 2 and the match.

games.decidingFactor: Power Patron survives Sky Striker’s longest resource loop and produces one final board wipe.

analysis: Power Patron won by presenting repeated waves of Extra Deck threats rather than relying on one board.
Sky Striker’s Link toolbox was used aggressively and meaningfully in both games.

matches.title: Toon Turbo vs. Dark Magician
context: This match is preserved as a detailed tactical archive. The exact original action-by-action transcript was not available during migration.

games.title: Game 1

turns.title: Toon setup
actions: Funny Dark Rabbit establishes Toon World the Perfect World and Comic Cat.
Toon Dark Magician and Evil Box extend the field and set Toon Terror.
turns.audit: The Extra Deck is preserved until the disruption has traded.
turns.endBoard: Toon Turbo establishes engine, information, and a negate.

turns.title: Dark Magician push
actions: Mind Scan preemptively suppresses Magician’s Rod.
Toon Terror and Dominus Impulse stop the follow-up involving Magicians’ Souls, Soul Servant, and Timaeus.
turns.audit: Toon prioritizes the cards that bridge Dark Magician’s Normal Summon into its Extra Deck.
turns.endBoard: Dark Magician’s turn is contained.

turns.title: Toon conversion
actions: Toon Turbo converts its remaining bodies into Dark Magician of Destruction, Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon, I:P Masquerena, and S:P Little Knight.
The layered board closes the game.
turns.audit: The Extra Deck is used after the opponent’s interaction is exhausted.
turns.endBoard: Toon Turbo wins Game 1.

games.decidingFactor: Mind Scan and the Toon traps stop the Dark Magician engine before Toon converts into Fusion and Link threats.

games.title: Game 2

turns.title: Dark Magician setup
actions: Dark Magical Circle, Magician’s Rod, Magicians’ Souls, and Timaeus establish two Level 7 bodies and Dark Magician of Destruction.
turns.audit: The deck identifies a higher-ceiling Rank 7 route rather than stopping at a conventional Dragoon board.
turns.endBoard: Two Level 7 monsters plus back-row support.

turns.title: Galaxy Tomahawk line
actions: Number 42: Galaxy Tomahawk creates enough material for I:P Masquerena and S:P Little Knight.
The line later pivots into Red-Eyes Dark Dragoon and Chaos Angel.
turns.audit: Dark Magician fully uses its Extra Deck instead of treating the archetype as only a Circle/Eternal Soul deck.
turns.endBoard: Dark Magician establishes multiple layers of disruption.

turns.title: Closing turns
actions: Toon Turbo attempts a defensive I:P line but cannot break through Dragoon and Chaos Angel.
Dark Magician wins Game 2.
turns.audit: No unnecessary further commitment is made once lethal is protected.
turns.endBoard: Match tied 1–1.

games.decidingFactor: The Galaxy Tomahawk Link line produces more interaction than Toon Turbo can answer.

games.title: Game 3

turns.title: Maximum Toon board
actions: Toon Turbo reaches Blue-Eyes Toon Ultimate Dragon, Dark Magician of Destruction, I:P Masquerena, Mind Scan, Toon Terror, Dominus Impulse, and Solemn Judgment.
turns.audit: The deck uses both Fusion and Link routes while retaining layered back-row interaction.
turns.endBoard: Toon Turbo establishes its strongest board of the match.

turns.title: Dark Magician counterplay
actions: Santa Claws removes Blue-Eyes Toon Ultimate Dragon.
Harpie’s Feather Duster and the Dark Magician engine attempt to dismantle the remaining field, but the layered responses hold.
turns.audit: Toon correctly protects its engine rather than overprotecting the already-replaced Fusion monster.
turns.endBoard: Dark Magician’s comeback is stopped.

turns.title: Lethal rebuild
actions: Comic Cat, Evil Box, S:P Little Knight, and W:P Fancy Ball rebuild the field.
Toon Turbo attacks for lethal.
turns.audit: The Extra Deck follow-up is used only after the board breakers have resolved.
turns.endBoard: Toon Turbo wins the match 2–1.

games.decidingFactor: Toon Turbo’s layered Game 3 board survives Santa Claws and Feather Duster, then rebuilds through its Link toolbox.

analysis: The corrected simulation treats Toon Turbo as a Fusion/Link deck rather than a Main-Deck-only Toon strategy.
Dark Magician’s best game came from recognizing the Galaxy Tomahawk route.

matches.title: Elfnote vs. Kewl Tune
context: Elfnote controls the center Main Monster Zone. Its Level 6 monsters Special Summon themselves there and rotate positions during the opponent’s turn to create interaction.
Kewl Tune is built almost entirely from Tuners. Its Main Deck monsters can use Tuners from the hand as Synchro Material, allowing rapid climbing while preserving field space.

games.title: Game 1

turns.title: Turn 1 — Kewl Tune
actions: Kewl Tune reveals Kewl Tune Rotary and Kewl Tune Mix in hand.
Rotary’s hand effect grants an additional Normal Summon of a Tuner.
Kewl Tune Normal Summons Mix. Mix activates to add a non-Level-2 Kewl Tune monster.
Elfnote responds with Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring. Chain Link 1: Mix; Chain Link 2: Ash Blossom. Mix is negated.
Kewl Tune uses its regular Normal Summon on Kewl Tune Cue. Cue Special Summons Rotary from the hand.
Cue and Rotary Synchro Summon Kewl Tune Track Maker.
Track Maker, Cue, and Rotary trigger. Rotary looks at Elfnote’s hand and adds Kewl Tune Synchro; Cue excavates and manipulates the top two cards of Elfnote’s Deck; Track Maker adds JJ “Kewl Tune”.
JJ “Kewl Tune” is activated. Track Maker uses Mix from the hand as Synchro Material to summon Kewl Tune Loudness War.
Kewl Tune Synchro adds Kewl Tune Reco, then the line produces Kewl Tune RS.
Kewl Tune sets its remaining interaction.
turns.audit: Kewl Tune declines an immediate climb into Kewl Tune B2B. Loudness War, RS, and a set Quick-Play Spell provide more separate interactions than one larger boss.
turns.endBoard: Kewl Tune: Loudness War, RS, JJ “Kewl Tune”, two set cards. Elfnote: empty field, four cards in hand.

turns.title: Turn 2 — Elfnote
actions: Elfnote Special Summons Elfnote Lucina to the center Main Monster Zone.
Lucina activates to search. Loudness War banishes Cue from the GY and copies Cue’s material effect, manipulating Elfnote’s next cards without negating Lucina.
Lucina resolves and adds Elfnote Regina.
Elfnote activates Elfnotes: Welcome Home. RS banishes Rotary and negates Welcome Home for the turn.
Elfnote Normal Summons Elfnote Power Patron and raises Lucina from Level 6 to Level 9.
Power Patron and Lucina Synchro Summon Elfnote June Pride. Power Patron’s GY effect adds Elfnotes: Rhapsodia of Madness.
June Pride returns itself to the Extra Deck and deploys Fortuna from hand, Tinia from Deck, and Lucina from GY.
Fortuna places Rhapsodia; Tinia places Welcome Home; Lucina searches.
Kewl Tune activates the set Kewl Tune Synchro, searches Kewl Tune Clip, and Synchro Summons Kewl Tune Crackle.
Crackle examines Elfnote’s Extra Deck, temporarily banishes Baronne de Fleur, and gains its ATK for the turn.
Elfnote sets Infinite Impermanence and Rhapsodia.
turns.audit: Returning June Pride to the Extra Deck is superior to leaving a single 3100 ATK body. Elfnote converts it into three distinct opponent-turn interactions plus continuous-card setup.
turns.endBoard: Elfnote: Tinia in the center, Lucina, Fortuna, Welcome Home, Rhapsodia, two set cards. Kewl Tune: Loudness War, RS, Crackle, JJ “Kewl Tune”, one set card.

turns.title: Turn 3 — Kewl Tune
actions: Tinia rotates with Fortuna and temporarily banishes Kewl Tune Reco from the hand.
Fortuna rotates with Lucina and returns JJ “Kewl Tune” to the hand.
Loudness War copies Mix’s material effect and targets Lucina for destruction.
Elfnote chains Rhapsodia, sending Regina to the GY to revive Lucina. Ghost Belle & Haunted Mansion negates Rhapsodia; Lucina remains in the GY.
JJ “Kewl Tune” Tributes RS and Special Summons Cue from the Deck.
Cue and Crackle produce Kewl Tune B2B. Crackle revives itself and temporarily banishes June Pride and Crystal Wing Synchro Dragon from Elfnote’s Extra Deck.
B2B raises the Levels of Elfnote’s monsters by 2, disrupting their preferred Synchro math.
Reco returns and is Normal Summoned, recovering Mix.
B2B destroys Fortuna in battle, attacks again, and destroys Tinia. Crackle attacks directly.
turns.audit: B2B is introduced only after Elfnote has spent several interactions. It is functioning as a second-stage boss rather than the opening end board.
turns.endBoard: Kewl Tune: B2B, Crackle, Reco, JJ “Kewl Tune”. Elfnote: Welcome Home, two Rhapsodia cards, Infinite Impermanence, no monsters.

turns.title: Turn 4 — Elfnote
actions: Elfnote Normal Summons Medius the Pure. B2B revives Cue and immediately converts Cue plus Crackle into Baronne de Fleur.
Medius resolves and Special Summons Junoldo the Shadespirit Power Patron from the Deck.
Welcome Home sends Medius to the GY and summons Elfnote Regina into the center zone.
Regina attempts to Special Summon Lucina. Baronne negates Regina and destroys it.
Rhapsodia sends Junoldo to the GY and revives Regina.
Infinite Impermanence negates B2B for the turn.
Regina destroys Reco in battle, but Reco’s material effect does not trigger because it was not used as Synchro Material.
turns.audit: Elfnote successfully trades through Baronne’s negate, but cannot turn the revived Regina into an Extra Deck threat because the required Tuner was spent as Rhapsodia’s cost.
turns.endBoard: Elfnote: Regina and continuous back row. Kewl Tune: B2B, Baronne, JJ “Kewl Tune”, Mix in hand.

turns.title: Turn 5 — Kewl Tune
actions: Baronne destroys Welcome Home.
Kewl Tune Synchro adds Rotary and immediately produces Track Maker using Rotary and Mix.
Mix destroys Regina; Rhapsodia attempts to revive it.
B2B revives Reco and converts Reco plus Track Maker into Loudness War.
Track Maker returns one Rhapsodia to hand; Reco destroys the other.
B2B attacks directly twice for lethal.
turns.audit: Kewl Tune sequences removal before the Battle Phase, eliminating both recursion cards so B2B’s double attack cannot be interrupted.
turns.endBoard: Game over.

games.decidingFactor: Loudness War and B2B converted Elfnote’s repeated effect activations into additional value and Synchro Summons.

games.title: Game 2

sideDeck.Elfnote: Adds Droll & Lock Bird, PSY-Framegear Gamma, PSY-Frame Driver, and more back-row disruption.
sideDeck.Kewl Tune: Adds more Spell/Trap removal, Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit, and going-second hand traps.

turns.title: Turn 1 — Elfnote
actions: Elfnote Special Summons Tinia to the center and places Welcome Home.
Ghost Ogre destroys Tinia after activation, so Welcome Home remains placed.
Welcome Home sends Regina to the GY and summons Lucina. Lucina searches Fortuna.
Fydraulis Harmonia Special Summons itself in response to Lucina’s monster effect, sends a revealed Synchro Monster to the GY, and destroys Lucina.
Elfnote Normal Summons Power Patron, then Special Summons Fortuna to the center. Fortuna places Rhapsodia.
Elfnote sets Rhapsodia and ends.
turns.audit: Elfnote preserves Fortuna and Power Patron instead of forcing a compromised Synchro line after Harmonia removes Lucina.
turns.endBoard: Elfnote: Fortuna, Power Patron, Welcome Home, set Rhapsodia. Kewl Tune: Harmonia.

turns.title: Turn 2 — Kewl Tune
actions: Rotary grants an extra Normal Summon. Mix searches Kewl Tune Clip.
Elfnote activates Droll & Lock Bird, preventing further additions from Deck to hand.
Cue Special Summons Rotary. Power Patron raises Fortuna and immediately Synchro Summons June Pride.
Droll prevents Power Patron’s GY search.
June Pride returns to the Extra Deck and deploys Tinia, Lucina, and Regina.
Tinia can still place a Continuous Spell and Regina can still Special Summon, because those actions do not add cards to the hand.
Cue and Rotary make Track Maker, but Droll suppresses Track Maker’s search.
Track Maker and Clip produce Loudness War. Clip permanently banishes a random Extra Deck card; Track Maker returns set Rhapsodia to hand.
Harmonia attacks Lucina; both are destroyed.
turns.audit: Droll does not stop Synchro Summoning, but strips the searches that normally make Kewl Tune’s climbing profitable.
turns.endBoard: Elfnote: Tinia, Regina, Fortuna, two Welcome Home cards. Kewl Tune: Loudness War and Mix.

turns.title: Turn 3 — Elfnote
actions: Tinia and Fortuna place additional Elfnote continuous cards.
Regina sends Rhapsodia to the GY and summons Lucina.
Welcome Home converts Fortuna into Power Patron.
Power Patron raises Tinia and Synchro Summons June Pride.
June Pride destroys Mix; Regina and Lucina attack directly.
Kewl Tune survives at 500 LP because June Pride’s center-zone attack restriction limits the remaining attacks.
turns.audit: Elfnote correctly leaves June Pride in the center this time. Its attack restriction protects the board while presenting near-lethal damage.
turns.endBoard: Elfnote: June Pride, Regina, Lucina, multiple continuous cards, set Infinite Impermanence. Kewl Tune: Loudness War.

turns.title: Turn 4 — Kewl Tune
actions: Kewl Tune Synchro adds Reco.
Infinite Impermanence negates Loudness War.
Reco is Normal Summoned and recovers Mix.
June Pride returns itself to the Extra Deck and redeploys three Elfnote monsters.
Lucina rotates into the center and returns Reco to the hand.
Kewl Tune concedes against overwhelming damage.
turns.audit: The defensive June Pride transformation removes Kewl Tune’s only new body while preserving lethal pressure.
turns.endBoard: Game over.

games.decidingFactor: Droll suppressed Kewl Tune’s search economy, allowing June Pride to control both tempo and combat.

games.title: Game 3

sideDeck.Kewl Tune: Adds anti-hand-trap protection, Ghost Belle, back-row removal, and resilient extenders.
sideDeck.Elfnote: Adds Ghost Ogre, Effect Veiler, Infinite Impermanence, and the PSY-Frame package.

turns.title: Turn 1 — Kewl Tune
actions: Rotary grants an extra Normal Summon. Mix is Normal Summoned and targeted by Infinite Impermanence.
PSY-Framegear Gamma cannot respond because Kewl Tune already controls Mix.
Reco is Normal Summoned and adds Cue.
Mix and Rotary produce Track Maker. Track Maker searches Kewl Tune Synchro; Rotary inspects Elfnote’s hand and adds JJ “Kewl Tune”.
Track Maker and Cue from hand produce Loudness War.
Two Kewl Tune Synchro activations develop Crackle and RS.
turns.audit: Kewl Tune again declines B2B, preferring Loudness War, Crackle, and RS as three distinct interactions.
turns.endBoard: Kewl Tune: Loudness War, Crackle, RS, JJ “Kewl Tune”, Gamma in hand.

turns.title: Turn 2 — Elfnote
actions: Lucina is Special Summoned to the center and activates.
Loudness War copies Mix and targets Lucina for destruction.
Welcome Home sends Lucina to the GY as cost and summons Tinia, causing the copied destruction to lose its target.
Lucina resolves and searches Fortuna; Tinia places another Welcome Home.
Power Patron targets Tinia, but RS negates Power Patron.
Regina is Special Summoned by sending Fortuna to the GY.
Welcome Home converts Regina into Fortuna, and Fortuna places Rhapsodia.
turns.audit: Elfnote uses Welcome Home as a dodge, but RS prevents the turn’s key immediate Synchro Summon.
turns.endBoard: Elfnote: Tinia, Fortuna, Power Patron, two Welcome Home cards, set Rhapsodia. Kewl Tune retains all three Synchro interactions.

turns.title: Turn 3 — Kewl Tune
actions: Tinia rotates with Fortuna and temporarily banishes Gamma from Kewl Tune’s hand.
Fortuna rotates with Power Patron and returns JJ “Kewl Tune” to hand.
Loudness War copies Reco and destroys the set Rhapsodia.
JJ Tributes Crackle and summons Cue. Crackle revives itself and temporarily banishes June Pride and Baronne from Elfnote’s Extra Deck.
Cue and Crackle produce B2B. Clip permanently banishes another random Extra Deck card.
B2B raises Elfnote’s monster Levels, disrupting future Synchro arithmetic.
B2B attacks twice, destroying Power Patron and Tinia. RS destroys Fortuna.
turns.audit: B2B enters after the first interaction layer has traded, then its Level modulation and double attack punish Elfnote’s exposed board.
turns.endBoard: Kewl Tune: B2B, Loudness War, RS, JJ “Kewl Tune”, Gamma in hand. Elfnote: two Welcome Home cards, no monsters.

turns.title: Turn 4 — Elfnote
actions: Welcome Home sends Regina to the GY and summons Lucina.
Gamma again cannot activate because Kewl Tune controls monsters.
Lucina activates. B2B revives Mix, then immediately Synchro Summons Baronne de Fleur using Mix and RS.
Mix’s material effect destroys Lucina; Lucina’s search still resolves.
The second Welcome Home is activated. Baronne negates and destroys it.
Elfnote has no remaining playable card.
turns.audit: B2B converts the first monster activation into Baronne while Mix’s material trigger removes the starter. This is the matchup’s clearest example of Kewl Tune generating two interactions from one response window.
turns.endBoard: Kewl Tune: B2B, Loudness War, Baronne, JJ “Kewl Tune”.

turns.title: Turn 5 — Kewl Tune
actions: Baronne destroys Elfnote’s final Welcome Home.
B2B attacks directly twice for lethal.
turns.audit: No further Extra Deck commitment is necessary.
turns.endBoard: Game over.

games.decidingFactor: Multiple separate Synchro interactions survived Elfnote’s opening push and converted into B2B plus Baronne.

analysis: Elfnote’s strongest use of June Pride is often its transformation effect, not its 3100 ATK body.
Kewl Tune performs best when B2B is treated as a second-stage boss after Loudness War, RS, and Crackle have already traded.
The matchup is structurally favorable to Kewl Tune when it goes first because Elfnote’s sequential monster effects repeatedly open response windows.

matches.title: Toon vs. Branded
context: The original result is excluded because Toon’s Maliss/Cyberse and other Extra Deck routes were underused.
analysis: This match will be replayed with an explicit Extra Deck audit at every major decision point.
